brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Conceptually inventive metaphor: mapping musical chord theory to color harmonies is a genuinely fresh, memorable system.
Three-panel layout cleanly separates controls, instrument, and output, giving the tool an immediate mental model.
Vivid HSL swatches plus the coral accent create a confident, playful identity aligned with the 'play colors' brief.
dominant_weaknesses: Piano rendering is crude — black keys overlap white-key labels (C#/D#) and the keyboard lacks tactile depth or active-key feedback.
Coral pink primary clashes with the generated blue/magenta/red palette below, undermining the harmony promise the tool itself preaches.
Static screenshot reveals no motion language — chord 'locking', key strikes, and palette transitions are the soul of the concept and invisible here.
fix_priorities: Redesign the keyboard: proper key proportions, label placement under white keys, and visible pressed/held states for chord lock.
Replace coral UI accent with a neutral or palette-derived accent so the chrome doesn't fight the generated colors.
Add motion specs — key depression, color burst on strike, palette swatch entrance — to make the musical metaphor felt.
Tighten typography hierarchy; section labels, slider values, and chord-mode buttons currently read at similar weights.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong reflective concept and decent visceral color, but behavioral execution (keyboard interaction, feedback) lags behind the idea.
rationale.intent_fit: The metaphor is delivered structurally, but without believable instrument feel and motion the 'play colors like music' promise reads more as diagram than instrument.
